pins.title: How Much Grass Seed Do I Need? (Chart + Free Calculator)
pins.description: Find out how many pounds of grass seed your lawn needs. This chart shows seed amounts for 5,000 sq ft and 1 acre at common label rates, and the free calculator works it out for your exact lawn size and seed bag.
pins.heading: How Much Grass Seed Do I Need?
pins.sub: Seed needed = label rate × lawn area. Find your rate on the seed bag.
pins.note: Rates vary by grass type and new lawn vs. overseeding. Add about 10% extra. 1 acre = 43,560 sq ft.

pins.title: How Many Pavers Do I Need? Pavers per 100 Sq Ft Chart
pins.description: Planning a DIY paver patio or walkway? See how many pavers you need per 100 square feet for 4x8, 6x6, 12x12, 16x16 and other sizes, plus a free paver calculator with waste allowance.
pins.heading: How Many Pavers Do I Need?
pins.sub: Pavers per 100 square feet for common paver sizes.
pins.note: Example: a 10 × 10 ft patio with 16 × 16 in pavers needs 57 pavers, or 62 with 10% extra.

pins.title: How Many Fence Posts Do I Need? Fence Post Chart
pins.description: Quick fence post chart for 50 to 300 ft fences at 6 ft and 8 ft spacing. Learn the simple formula (posts = sections + 1), how to space posts evenly, and when to add posts for corners and gates.
pins.heading: How Many Fence Posts Do I Need?
pins.sub: Posts for one straight fence run. Posts = sections + 1.
pins.note: Add extra posts for corners and gates. Spacing is the maximum; posts end up evenly spaced a little closer.

pins.title: How Many Bags of Concrete for a Slab? 80 lb Bag Chart
pins.description: How many 80 lb bags of concrete for a 4 inch slab? See bag counts for common slab sizes from 4x4 to 12x12, including 10% extra, then use the free concrete bag calculator for your own size and bag yield.
pins.heading: How Many Bags of Concrete for a 4 in Slab?
pins.sub: 80 lb bags, including 10% extra for waste.
pins.note: Assumes about 0.60 cu ft per 80 lb bag. Check the yield printed on your bag.

pins.title: How Much Gravel Do I Need? Cubic Yards and Tons Chart
pins.description: Gravel chart for common areas at 3 inches deep, in cubic yards and tons. Great for planning paths, patios and gravel beds. Use the free gravel calculator to enter your own size, depth and supplier density.
pins.heading: How Much Gravel Do I Need?
pins.sub: For a 3 in deep layer, including 10% extra.
pins.note: Weight assumes 105 lb per cubic foot. Ask your supplier for their gravel density.

pins.title: How Many Deck Boards Do I Need? Deck Board Chart
pins.description: Deck board counts for common deck sizes using 5.5 in boards with 1/8 in gaps, plus linear feet with 10% extra. Use the free deck board calculator for your own deck size, board width and gap.
pins.heading: How Many Deck Boards Do I Need?
pins.sub: 5.5 in boards, 1/8 in gaps. Boards run along the deck length.
pins.note: Board count is across the deck width. Buy boards at least as long as the deck, or plan joints over joists.

pins.title: How Many Pickets for a Fence Gate? Gate Width Chart
pins.description: How many 5.5 inch pickets does a wood fence gate need? This chart covers gates from 3 ft to 12 ft wide with a 1/8 inch gap, and the free gate calculator works it out for your own picket size.
pins.heading: How Many Pickets for a Fence Gate?
pins.sub: 5.5 in pickets with a 1/8 in gap between them.
pins.note: Double drive gates: use the total opening width. Frame, hinges and latch are extra.

pins.title: How Many Bags of Concrete for Deck Footings? (12 x 36 in)
pins.description: See how many 80 lb bags of concrete you need for 4 to 15 round deck footings, 12 inches wide and 36 inches deep, with 10% extra. Use the free deck footing calculator for your own hole size and frost depth.
pins.heading: How Many Concrete Bags for Deck Footings?
pins.sub: 12 in round holes, 36 in deep, 10% extra included.
pins.note: Assumes about 0.60 cu ft per 80 lb bag. Footing depth must meet your local frost line and code.

pins.title: How Much Concrete per Post Hole? 80 lb Bag Chart by Hole Size
pins.description: How many 80 lb bags of concrete does a post hole take? This chart shows bags for one hole and for 10 holes at common diameters and depths, with 10% extra. The free post hole calculator handles any size.
pins.heading: How Much Concrete per Post Hole?
pins.sub: 80 lb bags, 10% extra included. The post itself is not subtracted.
pins.note: Assumes about 0.60 cu ft per 80 lb bag. Bag counts are rounded up.

pins.title: How Much Base Gravel and Sand for a Paver Patio? Size Chart
pins.description: How much gravel base and bedding sand does a paver patio need? See amounts for patios from 10x10 to 16x20 ft with a 6 inch base and 1 inch of sand, then use the free paver base calculator for your own depths.
pins.heading: How Much Base and Sand for a Paver Patio?
pins.sub: 6 in gravel base and 1 in bedding sand, 10% extra included.
pins.note: Driveways and soft soil usually need a deeper base. Check the paver maker's guide.

pins.title: How Much Mulch Do I Need? Cubic Yards Chart by Bed Size
pins.description: How many cubic yards of mulch do you need? See amounts for garden beds from 50 to 500 sq ft at 2 and 3 inches deep, with 10% extra, then use the free mulch calculator for your exact beds.
pins.heading: How Much Mulch Do I Need?
pins.sub: Cubic yards of mulch, 10% extra included.
pins.note: 1 cubic yard = 27 cu ft. Keep mulch a few inches away from tree trunks and house siding.

pins.title: How Many Fence Panels Do I Need? Panels and Posts by Fence Length
pins.description: See how many 8 ft fence panels and posts you need for a 50 to 300 ft fence, with 10% extra panels to order. Use the free fence panel calculator for your exact fence length and panel width.
pins.heading: How Many Fence Panels Do I Need?
pins.sub: 8 ft wide panels on a straight run, 10% extra included.
pins.note: Posts = panels + 1 for one straight run. Add a post for each corner, end and gate.

pins.title: How Many Deck Boards Fit Across My Deck? Boards and Gap by Deck Width
pins.description: How many 5.5 in deck boards fit across a deck 8 to 20 ft wide with a 1/8 in gap, and what the real gap works out to. Use the free deck board spacing calculator for your own boards.
pins.heading: How Many Deck Boards Across My Deck?
pins.sub: 5.5 in wide boards (5/4x6 or 2x6) with a 1/8 in target gap.
pins.note: Width is measured across the joists. Check the board maker's gap rules: wet wood boards often go tight.

pins.title: How Much Concrete for a Driveway? Cubic Yards Chart by Size
pins.description: How many cubic yards of concrete does a driveway need? See amounts for common driveway sizes at 4 and 5 inches thick with 10% extra, then use the free concrete driveway calculator.
pins.heading: How Much Concrete for a Driveway?
pins.sub: Cubic yards to order, 10% extra included.
pins.note: Ready-mix is usually ordered in quarter or half yards. Check local code for driveway thickness and base.

pins.title: How Many Pavers for a 10x10, 12x12 or 16x20 Patio? (Chart)
pins.description: See how many 12x12 and 16x16 pavers you need for common patio sizes, with 10% extra for cuts and breakage. The free paver calculator works it out for any patio and paver size.
pins.heading: How Many Pavers for My Patio?
pins.sub: Pavers to order, 10% extra for cuts included.
pins.note: Uses nominal paver size. Curves, borders and herringbone patterns need more extra.

pins.title: How Much Gravel for a Driveway? Cubic Yards and Tons Chart
pins.description: How much gravel do you need for a gravel driveway 4 inches deep? See cubic yards and tons for common driveway sizes, with 10% extra, then use the free driveway gravel calculator.
pins.heading: How Much Gravel for My Driveway?
pins.sub: 4 in deep, 10% extra included, 105 lb per cu ft.
pins.note: Gravel density varies by stone type. Ask your supplier for its weight per cubic yard.
